messages:
ops-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: node node-ssd-12 ephemeral-storage > 94% and PodEvicted events increasing. Auto-created incident thread.

Maya (oncall): grabbing this. Seeing repeated Evicted events for modelcache-daemonset and serve-runtime pods on node-ssd-12. Clients hitting 503/500 for a subset of requests.

Liam (sre): confirmed via kubelet logs: "Eviction manager: attempting to reclaim ephemeral-storage" then multiple "Pod \"modelcache-...\": eviction" lines. Journal shows heavy write rates from /var/lib/modelcache and /var/log/gptx-serve logs.

Anya (eng-runtime): got a stacktrace from a restarted runtime: "open /var/lib/modelcache/opt/llama2/weights.part: no space left on device" and then a SIGABRT when trying to mmap. Model loader crashes on missing files, kube restarts, modelcache tries to recover and ends up writing more temp files => feedback loop.

Maya (oncall): immediate mitigation options: 1) cordon node-ssd-12, 2) shift user traffic to fallback pool, 3) drain non-critical workload, 4) temporary reduce modelcache retention and disable prefetch. Liam, can you cordon and start cleanup? Anya, prepare runtime guard config. Jordan/Sam, prepare customer comms.

Liam (sre): on it. Running:
```
kubectl cordon node-ssd-12
kubectl drain node-ssd-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=5m
ssh admin@node-ssd-12 'sudo du -sh /var/lib/modelcache/* /var/log/gptx-serve/* | sort -rh | head -n 30'
```
Found: older-models/llama2-v1 (140GB), tmp/gptx-stream (90GB), debug/logs (60GB).

deploy-bot: :white_check_mark: apply patch to modelcache DaemonSet env MODELCACHE_MAX_VERSIONS=1 to reduce retention on canary nodes.

Anya (eng-runtime): rolling a small runtime patch to gate background downloads: if available disk < 12% then modelcache returns 503 for prefetch ops and runtime will fallback to on-demand streaming. Also add liveness backoff to avoid immediate crash loops when mmap fails. Pushing to canary.

deploy-bot: canary update applied to inference-canary-1 and inference-canary-2.

Liam (sre): cleanup actions performed: rotated gptx logs, deleted stale model dirs older than 30d, cleared /tmp artifacts. Reclaimed ~260GB. Ran `systemctl restart kubelet` to ensure node notices freed space. Disk usage decreased to ~58%.

stacktrace-bot: attached aggregated crash log snippet:
```
runtime: panic: open /var/lib/modelcache/opt/llama2/weights.part: no space left on device
goroutine 1 [running]:
main.loadModel(0x7ffdf...)
\t/app/loader/loader.go:214 +0x23a
```

Jordan (support): We're seeing 6 customer-reported errors and an internal spike in failed embeddings. Latency for affected requests up to 6-8s before 503. Ticket count increased by 4 in last 20m. Draft status: "Degraded inference for subset of US-east requests; we have routed traffic and are cleaning affected node; mitigations in progress." Suggestions?n

Sam (customer-success): That wording is fine. Recommend including ETA: 30-45m and mention that we have a rollback path if issues persist. I'll flag high-touch customers.

Maya (oncall): Posting to status page now: "Investigating degraded inference performance in US-east due to node storage pressure causing pod evictions. Traffic shifted to fallback pool; mitigating. ETA 30-45m." Jordan publish when ready.

Liam (sre): Observed no new PodEvicted events after cleanup and cordon. Started uncordon test for a small subset of pods after applying MODELCACHE_MAX_VERSIONS=1 canary. Monitoring file churn.

Anya (eng-runtime): After canary, modelcache stopped keeping multiple versions and prefetchs are gated. Runtime no longer crashes on cold loads because prefetch deferred until space available. Added a temporary disk-check: on startup if free < 8% runtime fails fast and signals admin rather than attempting aggressive writes. Will follow up with a safer fallback design.

Maya (oncall): Handoff: I'm handing this to Liam for the 1:1 follow-up and postmortem. Handoff in 40m. Summary for postmortem: root cause = aggressive model prefetch + multi-version retention + unbounded debug log writes + insufficient node-level journald retention; effect = disk exhaustion -> pod eviction -> runtime crash loops -> customer errors. Preliminary mitigations = traffic failover, cordon+cleanup, MODELCACHE_MAX_VERSIONS=1, prefetch gating.

Liam (sre): Postmortem action items (initial): 1) enforce default MODELCACHE_MAX_VERSIONS=2 and make it configurable per-customer, 2) admission controller to prevent pod scheduling that would exceed node disk reservation, 3) journald/logrotate limits on inference nodes, 4) runtime backoff on mmap failures and better telemetry for disk pressure.

Sam (customer-success): Sending customer update: "Mitigation complete for most customers; we routed traffic and reclaimed node storage. Some customers may have experienced transient errors. We will share a full postmortem within 48 hours."

Maya (oncall): Closing active pager. Keeping a watch for 1h. Ping @oncall if Evicted events reappear. :thumbsup:
